findings.evidence: Basic.lean:21 `abbrev Face {ι : Type*} (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) := {σ : Finset ι // σ ∈ K}`; Subdivision.lean:62 the identical body for `PreAbstractSimplicialComplex`. Mathlib's `mem_toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex` (Basic.lean:27-29) is `Iff.rfl`, so `Face K` and `BarycentricVertex K.toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex` are definitionally the same type.
findings.fix: Define the general `PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.Face K := {σ : Finset α // σ ∈ K}` in `Basic.lean`, delete `AbstractSimplicialComplex.Face` and `BarycentricVertex`, and update the uses in `Realization.lean` (lines 87, 95, 103, 106, 108, 115, 256, 412) and `Simplex/Realization.lean:53`. `barycentricSubdivision K` then reads `orderComplex K.Face`.
findings.issue: `abbrev BarycentricVertex (K : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex α) := {σ : Finset α // σ ∈ K}` is the same subtype as the existing `AbstractSimplicialComplex.Face K := {σ : Finset ι // σ ∈ K}` (Basic.lean:21), just at the more general `PreAbstractSimplicialComplex` level. The PR adds a second, application-specific name instead of moving the existing definition to the general level, leaving two names for one concept and tying the general construction to one use (barycentric subdivision).

findings.evidence: OrderComplex.lean:83-86 and 97-99 are the same three-line case split; Mathlib has no `IsChain`-plus-reflexivity comparability lemma (`grep -rn "IsChain.total" Mathlib/` returns nothing), so the general statement is not already available.
findings.fix: Move `comparable_of_mem_orderComplex` above `pair_mem_orderComplex_iff` and prove the forward direction as `comparable_of_mem_orderComplex h (by simp) (by simp)`. The reflexive-comparability step (`IsChain (· ≤ ·) s → p ∈ s → q ∈ s → p ≤ q ∨ q ≤ p`) is a fact about chains in a preorder with no simplicial content, so it is worth isolating as such.
findings.issue: The forward direction of `pair_mem_orderComplex_iff` (lines 83-86) repeats verbatim the `by_cases hpq : p = q` / `Or.inl hpq.le` / apply-the-chain argument of `comparable_of_mem_orderComplex` (lines 97-99); the pair case is a special case of the general one, which is stated later in the file.

summary: The order-complex layer sits at a good level, but `BarycentricVertex` re-introduces, under a new name, the face subtype that already exists as `AbstractSimplicialComplex.Face` — the PR needs the strictly more general `PreAbstractSimplicialComplex` version and should generalize the existing definition rather than add a parallel one. A special-case proof is also duplicated between `pair_mem_orderComplex_iff` and `comparable_of_mem_orderComplex`.
